nd6870fce4a78: Jiang et al. show that Akkermansia muciniphila reshapes the tumor immune environment to overcome PD-1 resistance in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer (MSS CRC). Mechanistic studies and a phase 1 trial support gut microbiome modulation as a promising strategy to improve immunotherapy in this common treatment-resistant disease.
n9136ccfb3367: Li et al. show that activated CAR-T cells upregulate NKG2D ligands (NKG2DLs), rendering them susceptible to NK cells. Overexpressing NKG2D shields endogenous ligands and harnesses tumor NKG2DLs for costimulation, thereby enhancing CAR-T cell persistence, tumor infiltration, and antitumor efficacy across multiple models.
nb03ad83957ab: Liu et al. demonstrate that high membrane magnesium transporter 1 (MMGT1) expression promotes immune evasion via a senescence-associated secretory phenotype that induces CD8+ T cells exhaustion. Targeting MMGT1 represents a promising strategy to improve anti-PD-1 immunotherapy efficacy.
nf2ef18422680: Wang et al. generate vascularized pancreatic islet organoids (VPIOs) containing organotypic vascular networks exhibiting endothelial fenestration. Vascularization enhances β cell maturation in vitro and survival under hypoxia. Following transplantation into diabetic mice, VPIOs establish functional connections with the host vasculature and effectively restore normoglycemia.
n5a881812522f: Ginhoux, Mulder, Arcila-Barrera, and Amit argue that macrophage identity is best understood not as a set of discrete subsets or a binary M1/M2 axis but as combinations of modular gene programs. They propose an extensible, program-based classification of macrophage states and discuss how it reframes macrophage-directed therapy from targeting individual checkpoints toward program-level reprogramming.
nc9f8f2a7a2d7: Srivastava et al. show that de novo-designed protein binders can selectively recognize the closed state of HSP90. The binders stabilize this conformation and provide new tools to study the HSP90 chaperone cycle and suggest a potential approach to HSP90 inhibition.
nfb8e8d3df4dc: Carbon dioxide (CO2) is a bioactive gas essential for several physiologically important biological processes, including metabolism, acid–base homoeostasis, and chemosensing. CO2 can directly modulate these processes by stimulating or inhibiting specific cell signalling pathways, including the nuclear factor-κB, calcium, and Wingless (Wnt) pathways. One mechanism by which CO2 interacts with proteins to modulate cell signalling is through the reversible and nonenzymatic modification of α- N-terminal and lysine ε-amino groups to form the carbamate post-translational modification (PTM). Identifying carbamate PTMs is technically challenging because these modifications are readily reversible. However, emerging techniques have now made possible their identification and functional characterisation. Here, we review recent advances in experimental and computational methods to identify CO2-mediated PTMs.
nfc2fa81c3b99: Enzyme function is multidimensional, condition-dependent, and difficult to map at scale. Enzyme proximity sequencing (EP-Seq) is a deep mutational scanning method that combines a barcoded enzyme library, yeast surface display, fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS), and high-throughput DNA sequencing to measure enzyme expression and catalytic activity.
n444578e6d824: By studying nearly half a million human genomes, this work shows that structural variants, large changes in DNA sequence greater than 50 base pairs, are an important and previously underrecognized source of human disease risk. The resulting resource reveals rare and regulatory structural variants linked to disease, providing insights into human biology and accelerating the development of medicines.
n3b869d82819c: Azo-morphine-3 (AM-3) is a photoswitchable ligand that toggles between low and high efficacy states to control mu-opioid receptor activity in vitro and in vivo both in the brain and periphery. AM-3 provides a powerful tool to probe the structural basis of opioid efficacy and enables spatiotemporally precise control of analgesia across pain models with reduced side effects compared with systemic drugs.
n85461ea325e3: Local cell-cell interactions give rise to emergent cellular patterns that encode ferroptosis-sensitive and -resistant fates and establish polarized lipid organization within cells. These coupled biochemical and biophysical properties enable self-organized cell populations to orient and confine otherwise isotropic, unbounded ferroptosis propagation, revealing a systems-level mechanism that regulates collective cell fate.
ncbd026f4cd08: Coleoid cephalopods edit their RNA at a level far beyond other animals, but the functional consequences to the proteome have been largely unknown. Proteomic detection of recoded sites reveals that single amino acid edits alter protein stability, subcellular localization, post-translational modification, and organelle function.
n775232b8c8e0: Pan et al. report tetraoxane-containing compounds WMK-1/2 as first-generation mitochondrial lipid peroxidation inducers that bypass GPX4- and retinol-mediated defenses to trigger a distinct “mito-ferroptosis” sub-pathway, demonstrating potent bioavailable tumor-suppressive activity across multiple in vivo models.
nd46b3bb0e829: A 22-tissue multi-omics atlas of chronic exercise is generated, detailing tissue-, sex-, and time-dependent molecular adaptations and cell-type-specific epigenetic remodeling in skeletal muscle. The atlas reveals coordinated transcriptomic, epigenetic, proteomic, and metabolic remodeling across the body.
nd7cb15e418f6: Kong et al. present a comprehensive resource for benchmarking somatic variant detection across variant classes and allele fractions. Using HapMap mixtures and pangenome graphs, they establish standardized benchmarking sets for evaluating sequencing technologies and variant-calling methods.
n99aa8f82a6de: Ha et al. benchmark detection strategies for mosaic mutations with low variant allele fractions (VAFs) using short- and long-read whole-genome sequencing. By cross-validating Illumina-based calls against PacBio HiFi data using cell-line mixtures generated across five institutions, they construct stratified reference sets, define realistic detection limits, and establish best practices for genome-wide analysis of low-VAF (<2%) variants in non-cancer tissues.
nb3f3b8a0e865: Lana Mediavilla et al. present NeoBridge, a biophysics-informed machine learning ensemble that prioritizes immunogenic neoantigens. In pancreatic cancer, subclonal neoantigen load, not clonal load, associates with worse survival, suggesting that clonal architecture should inform vaccine target selection
n3473663798ae: Qu et al. show that the Akkermansia muciniphila (AKK) protects against endometritis by promoting production of the microbial metabolite tyrosol, which reaches the uterus and suppresses inflammation. These findings reveal a metabolite-mediated gut-uterus axis linking the intestinal microbiota to reproductive health.
na9d16e158b7b: Meyers, Medina Evora, Molina Tijeras, et al. show that the colorectal cancer-associated oral bacterium Gemella morbillorum (Gm) promotes tumor progression. Colonization of the colon by Gm increases intestinal permeability, enables epithelial cell invasion, reshapes host lipid metabolism, and triggers DNA damage, collectively accelerating disease progression.
n2c6683ad4213: Predicting which patients will benefit from cancer immunotherapy remains challenging. Braun et al. use live tumor tissue from routine needle and forceps biopsies to measure ex vivo immunotherapy response. Results are consistent with clinical outcomes in a small patient cohort, including patients misclassified by current biomarker tests.
na92fadf8eee5: Wang et al. demonstrate that high-current transcranial temporal interference stimulation targeting sgACC alleviates depression safely and delivers stronger short-term therapeutic effects than low-current or sham stimulation.
nd6bebe49f738: Akay et al. use a genome-wide CRISPR screen to identify Wnt signaling as a regulator of lipid accumulation in APOE4 oligodendrocytes. Stimulating Wnt signaling by inhibiting GSK3B reduced lipid droplets and improved myelination in iPSC-derived brain organoids and APOE4;PS19 mice.
nee552d79d25c: Guo et al. develop a multiplex lineage-tracing platform to systematically profile fibroblasts across all five anatomical layers of the skin. They uncover a highly coordinated, multi-stage sequence of fibroblast mobilization and architectural reorganization during wound healing, demonstrating that cell-intrinsic programs predominate over local microenvironments to govern layer-specific contributions.
n302cf0a48a7a: Daniel L. Kastner, physician-scientist, geneticist, mentor, and scientific leader, transformed our understanding of human inflammatory disease. His death is a profound loss not only to the immunology community but also to the numerous patients and families whose illnesses he elucidated—and for whom, in many cases, he developed effective treatments. Called the “father of autoinflammatory diseases,” Dan did more than discover individual disorders: he defined an entirely new category of human disease.
n028466f3b40e: Metabolic reprogramming regulates immune cell function; however, how metabolic signals instruct early monocyte fate commitment remains unclear. Yang et al. show that LDHA-dependent cytosolic NAD+ regeneration promotes selective HIF1α translation, supporting commitment to a protective NOS2+ macrophage fate and revealing a broader link between redox metabolism and cell fate decisions.
n856af4ff701e: Qin et al. demonstrate that extrachromosomal DNA hubs function as inherent electrochemical reactors. By non-enzymatically generating a localized antioxidant shield, these hubs protect themselves from oxidative damage. Disrupting this spatial redox balance triggers ecDNA degradation, exposing a distinct vulnerability in ecDNA-positive cancers.
nc1cdbc532110: Müller, Kolesnikova, Doudin, et al. reveal a structural mechanism for residue-specific nucleosome acetylation by capturing the MSL histone acetyltransferase during catalysis. Their findings provide a foundation for understanding how H4K16 acetylation links transcription to changes in chromatin structure, a mechanism essential for Drosophila dosage compensation and implicated in human disease.
ndda0bb09677c: Lyu et al. show that the interaction between the deubiquitinase OTULIN and the ubiquitin ligase LUBAC restrains LUBAC autoubiquitination and activity. Disrupting this interaction enhances Met1-linked ubiquitination at the TNF receptor complex, which increases NF-κB signaling and sensitizes mice to TNF-dependent toxicity. Thus, the OTULIN-LUBAC interaction restricts Met1-linked ubiquitin signaling.
nc4620e7122b1: A weakness in glycobiology research is the insufficient integration of approaches used to connect glycan structure to function. From glycogene knockouts to understanding glycan structures, dynamics, and interactions, to determining whether a single glycan structure underlies a specific cellular function, no single approach provides sufficient information to establish these relationships. We argue that resolving glycan structure–function relationships requires the integration of complementary approaches spanning genetics, analytical glycomics, glycoengineering, structural biology, and computational modelling. The field stands at a transition point: from cataloguing glycan structures to understanding their diverse roles in regulating the biology of health and disease. Such an integrated approach will be critical for translating structural glycan information into mechanistic insights and, ultimately, informed glycoengineering and therapeutic design.
n249258f20d07: In Arabidopsis, pseudoenzyme class II T6P synthase functions as a T6P sensor that directly represses the master metabolic regulator SnRK1, highlighting a conserved switch that couples carbon availability to metabolic homeostasis in plants.
n28047ded39fc: Phenotype measurement scale has long been known to impact genetic inference, yet it is often ignored in modern studies. Costantino et al. characterize how the choice of phenotype scale affects the results of common analyses. They find that it can change GWAS hits and PGS × E interactions and influence PGS performance in specific subgroups.
n4b53e510b405: Gao et al. identify protein kinase (PKR) as a non-canonical stimulator of interferon genes (STING) effector in lung ischemia-reperfusion injury. STING oligomerization at the endoplasmic reticulum drives PKR-S33 autophosphorylation and TBK1-independent IKK-NF-κB activation. This pathway induces LAMP3-dependent lysosomal cell death, and its inhibition attenuates epithelial injury.
nd7eab5a7939f: Why does performance pressure sometimes cause choking but sometimes elicit exceptional performance? We propose that pressure shifts the complexity of information-processing rules that guide action. Performance improves when shifts move processing toward task-matched complexity and deteriorates when they promote maladaptive simplification, overcomplexification, or the use of rules that exceed available processing resources.
nd3b305961c8f: Bats use their hand-like wings to reproduce natural flights with wingbeat-level precision. Rather than mainly tracking the wingbeat cycle, the wing motor cortex generates sparse, distinct population states with little shared variance across wingbeats, resulting in a high-dimensional code distinct from that typically observed in constrained tasks.
n2a01732cc6c8: High-resolution real-time imaging of enhancer-promoter communication reveals how the two genomic loci are actively brought together through cohesin-mediated loop extrusion and how E-P interactions are temporally coordinated with transcriptional bursts. Unexpectedly, components of the RNA Pol II general machinery form nanoscale clusters at distal enhancers, and embedding the promoter into such clusters boosts GTF activities and triggers burst initiation.
nf0f8318ec4c4: Tetanus neurotoxin enters the central nervous system through motor neurons. This study identifies PTPRS as the long-sought retrograde transport receptor that directs toxin trafficking in motor neurons into the spinal cord, uncovering a host pathway that can be targeted for post-exposure treatment and for drug delivery into the central nervous system.
n352689535a20: By defining centromere haplogroups from rare k-mer variation, Shiraishi et al. uncover extensive hidden diversity and link centromere structure to human evolution and disease-associated genomic instability.
nd9d7d6cec6b0: Oladeji et al. determined the cryo-EM structure of the TccCas13a ternary complex and leveraged structural insights to engineer a thermophilic Cas13a variant with 100-fold enhanced sensitivity. The engineered nuclease retains programmability and thermostability, enabling highly sensitive RNA detection in different biological matrices.
n577324ec4e19: Yang and colleagues show that low-intensity priming during rapid chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T manufacturing preserves T cell fitness while restraining inflammatory programming. PrimeCAR cells maintain stemness-associated and proliferative responses with reduced myeloid-activating inflammation, and early-phase studies in B cell malignancies demonstrate encouraging clinical activity with few severe cytokine release syndrome (CRS) or immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) events.
n232536a222ef: Yuan et al. establish a scalable single-cell CRISPR platform in primary human HSPCs, linking 322 regulator perturbations to cell states and gene programs. The atlas identifies regulators associated with long-term repopulation and lineage-biased outputs and nominates PRDM10 as a candidate AML dependency.
n89e6ec2dfce9: Bai et al. reveal a PARP1-mediated m6A feedback mechanism involving IGF2BPs and the METTL3/METTL14 writer complex. They further show that combined targeting of ADP ribosylation and m6A leads to synergistic anti-tumor effects, providing a potential therapeutic strategy for cancer treatment.
n3cd9da96f6d5: Retrons help bacteria defend against phage by initiating a toxic response to restrict viral propagation. Here, Zhang et al. describe the non-canonical mechanism of Retron-Vpa2, which accumulates msDNA in response to phage triggers and regulates its toxic response on a translational level through a highly structured hybrid RNA.
n038f844d330f: Shin et al. present cryo-EM structures of the SPβ integrase along the integration and excision pathways that provide mechanistic insights addressing the long-standing questions of how large serine integrases enforce highly directional DNA recombination and how the cognate recombination directionality factor leads to a complete reversal of directionality.
n20f04c827951: Li et al. systematically map splicing within and between transposable elements (TEs) across cancers and define TEtrans, a tumor-enriched class of gene-independent transcripts. TEtrans display distinct regulatory programs and can function as oncogenic RNAs or encode immunogenic tumor antigens, expanding the functional landscape of TE reactivation in cancer.
n5d58caad6e4e: Lung cancer is a heterogeneous disease, and while targeted therapies and immunotherapies have improved patient outcomes, 5-year overall survival remains poor at approximately 20%. Antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) target tumors using a targeted antibody that delivers a cytotoxic payload with clinically proven antitumor activity, and over a dozen ADCs are under consideration for solid tumors. Recent clinical trial data in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer have led to FDA approval of three ADCs: trastuzumab deruxtecan for patients with human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-mutated disease, telisotuzumab vedotin for MET-overexpressing tumors, and datopotamab deruxtecan for patients with epidermal growth factor receptor-mutated disease. In this article, we review the trajectory of individual ADC targets in lung cancer, describe the latest clinical trial results, and discuss future innovations in ADC therapies and potential mechanisms of resistance.
nbd63ddd156f9: Höppner et al. show that disease-associated substitutions in PTH1R helix-8 selectively rewire receptor coupling to G proteins and βarrestin. Distinct mutations bias PTH1R engagement toward either Gαq or βarrestin pathways and impair Gαs activation. These findings reveal mutation-driven shifts in effector selectivity as a previously unrecognized mechanism in PTH1R-associated disease.
n718909ec8591: Wang et al. develop an oral metabolically engineered bacterial platform (EcN-HlpA-CGL [EHC]) for colorectal cancer immunotherapy, which triggers ferroptosis in colorectal cancer cells to boost immunogenicity, while the bacterial adjuvanticity reshapes the immunosuppressive microenvironment. This approach activates both systemic and gut mucosal immunity, effectively suppressing orthotopic tumor growth and metastasis.
nf3a2a5dfdcc8: Tissue-resident memory T (TRM) cells are heterogeneous, but how pathogenic subsets drive relapse in allergic dermatitis remains unclear. Asahina et al. identify a pathogenic CXCR6+ CD4+ TRM subset sustained through CXCL16-dependent clustering with CD301b+ cDC2s, revealing the TRM-DC niche as a potential therapeutic target for allergic dermatitis.
n6bc218949b2c: How metabolic enzyme levels are regulated is poorly understood. Studying the tryptophan (Trp)-metabolizing enzyme TDO2, Thielen et al. discover a CK2 kinase-β-TrCP E3 ligase pathway that regulates stability in response to substrate availability. Trp occupation of an exosite restricts degron accessibility, whereas low Trp releases the degron for phosphorylation-ubiquitylation-mediated degradation.
n695f93081a8a: Liang et al. identify phytanoyl-CoA dioxygenase domain containing 1 (PHYHD1) as a tumor suppressor that regulates protein production in kidney cancer. Loss of PHYHD1 promotes disease progression by increasing ceramide transporter 1 (CERT1) production, uncovering a regulatory pathway that may help predict patient outcomes and provide a therapeutic opportunity for PHYHD1-deficient tumors.
nf720614dfc33: Bonsor et al. determined the crystal structure of the KRAS-BRAF(RBD-CRD) complex, revealing reduced KRAS engagement by BRAF(CRD) compared with CRAF(CRD). They further show that the BRAF-specific region (BSR) attenuates RBD binding to KRAS, while inclusion of the CRD partially relieves this inhibition.
nf50730d9c221: Predictions of cysteine reactivity rely heavily on acidity (pKa) data from dilute solutions. However, the intracellular milieu is crowded and dynamic, with substrates, cofactors, and metabolites that modulate reactivity, thereby affecting cell signaling and metabolic adaptation. This forum argues that Cys pKa values are necessary but insufficient, proposing an integrated, microenvironment-dependent framework.
nc7255fb8e658: RNA fingerprinting is a statistical framework that infers causal regulators from single-cell experiments by mapping their transcriptional responses onto reference perturbation dictionaries.
n339bcbe92910: Chromatin reader inhibitors require robust cellular assays for target-engagement profiling. Recchia et al. develop modular Acyl-eCR reporters that enable scalable live-cell measurement of bromodomain inhibitor specificity and PROTAC activity, providing a versatile platform for chromatin-targeted drug discovery.
n9a51659ed626: The release of bacterial bioactive molecules across the gut barrier is a crucial yet poorly understood step in host-microbe communication. Here, we identify a phage-driven mechanism associated with this process in the beneficial symbiont Lactiplantibacillus plantarum NC8 (LpNC8). We show that a stress-responsive prophage, pp2, undergoes activation and triggers holin-lysin-mediated bacterial lysis, leading to the production of infectious phage particles and increased extracellular recovery of bacterial vesicles carrying lipoteichoic acids. In a model of nutritional symbiosis, pp2-dependent lysis is required for LpNC8 to promote juvenile growth in undernourished Drosophila melanogaster. Disruption of prophage-mediated lysis impairs vesicle recovery and host growth promotion. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the copper cell region of the Drosophila midgut acts as a physiological trigger of prophage induction. Together, our findings link host intestinal physiology to prophage activity and bacterial lysis, revealing phage-driven lysis as a mechanism contributing to beneficial bacterial-host interactions during nutritional stress.
nb43785e83752: DNA motif discovery and, particularly, computational modeling of transcription factor binding motifs, has been a mecca of algorithmic bioinformatics for several decades. Here, we report the results of the largest open community challenge in Inferring BInding Specificities (IBIS), where participants all over the world were invited to construct binding specificity models from multi-assay experimental data for poorly studied human transcription factors. The submissions were rigorously tested against a rich held-out dataset. Benchmarking demonstrated a consistent advantage of properly designed deep learning models over traditional positional weight matrices and other machine learning methods. Yet, the positional weight matrices displayed a surprisingly strong performance out of the box, being only slightly behind the best deep learning models. A post-challenge assessment of a selection of other deep learning methods further solidified this finding. IBIS highlights the power of benchmarking in finding adequate DNA motif representations, emphasizes the pros and cons of various machine learning methods applied to DNA motif modeling, and establishes a rich dataset, benchmarking protocols, and computational framework for a fair cross-platform evaluation of future models of transcription factor binding motifs in DNA sequences.
n3623de86684d: Symmans et al. review how artificial intelligence supports RNA therapeutic development in precision oncology, spanning multi-omics target prioritization and RNA design to delivery, patient stratification, manufacturing, and clinical translation. They distinguish clinically supported applications from preclinical and speculative approaches, outlining validation, governance, and regulatory requirements.
n93ed1f40f36f: Citrano, Maheswari Jawahar et al. develop sensitive immunoassays using second-generation polyclonal and monoclonal antibodies against HDGFL2-CE proteins and show that their levels in brain tissue associate with pTDP-43 pathology, earlier symptom onset, and shorter survival in patients with FTLD-TDP and FTLD-TDP/MND.
n1236e016d64e: Cabello-Yeves et al. use longitudinal metagenomic analysis of mother-infant dyads to show that infant gut phageomes diversify during the first year of life and are associated with feeding-related variables and maternal microbial reservoirs. Persistent bifidophages dominate early communities, highlighting the potential relevance of phages in microbiome-targeted early-life interventions.
n2459946c13b1: Zhao et al. show that circulating TCDCA associates with Parkinson’s disease severity and that TCDCA administration worsens neurovascular and motor outcomes in mice. VSMC TGR5 deletion and BSH-active L. reuteri interventions implicate a microbiota-regulated TCDCA-BBB pathway while defining its translational limitations.
nb2dff07df845: Klich et al. use a hydrogel to deliver immunotherapy combinations intratumorally and peritumorally. Rational selection of the site of administration drives tumor clearance and long-term survivors.
ncfb38586f394: Lymphatic vessel networks remodel during infection to regulate antigen and immune cell dynamics, yet whether these changes impact humoral immunity remains unknown. Mudianto et al. demonstrate that lymph node lymphangiogenesis encapsulates activating germinal centers to constrain their size, which enhances clonal selection and protective antibody responses, establishing lymphatic vessels as structural determinants of germinal center fitness.
nbb50e569c598: Terekhova et al. assemble a single-cell PBMC atlas of 8 datasets, 2,609 individuals, and over 12 million cells to dissect variable and conserved features of human immune aging. CD8+ Tem GZMK+ to GZMB+ ratio distinguishes healthy from disease-associated trajectories and predicts mortality risk. This work provides a clinically relevant marker for monitoring human aging.
n6591ddf170c1: Translational perturbations trigger ubiquitination and turnover of 40S ribosomes, yet how these events are coupled remains unclear. Shah et al. reveal that RIOK3 remodels ubiquitinated 40S subunits, exposing the 3′ end of 18S rRNA for uridylation and subsequent DIS3L2-mediated degradation. These findings link ribosomal protein ubiquitination to selective rRNA turnover.
nb1e417dab41f: 40S ribosomes are degraded in diverse stress conditions. Diehl et al. find that in response to stress, TUT7 is recruited to ubiquitylated 40S ribosomes and adds 3′ oligo(U) tails to the 18S rRNA. Iterative uridylation and 3′-5′ decay by the exonuclease DIS3L2 drive 18S rRNA and ultimately 40S ribosome degradation.
n6ba87c7edd62: Protein phosphorylation is a central and reversible mechanism regulating virtually all cellular processes and is classically mediated by the canonical protein kinome and phosphatome. However, beyond their traditional roles as metabolic catalysts, a subset of metabolic enzymes also exhibits noncanonical ‘moonlighting’ activities as protein kinases or phosphatases, directly linking metabolic states to phosphorylation-dependent signaling. These unexpected functions of enzymes involved in glucose, fructose, lipid, nucleotide, and creatine metabolism influence a broad spectrum of cellular processes, including chromatin remodeling, transcription, cell cycle progression, metabolism, autophagy, cell survival and death, and immune responses. As a result, metabolic enzymes are increasingly recognized as key regulators that bridge cellular metabolism and signaling networks, with important implications for both normal physiology and disease.
n2d7c6f852080: Organoids grown side by side under identical conditions vary unpredictably, a longstanding obstacle to their use. Adapting the logic of a classic fluctuation test to gastruloids grown from single stem cells shows that this variability is largely inherited rather than induced and is traceable to fluctuations in the state of the founding cell.
n9c3f0d80a839: Arabidopsis coordinates Fe acquisition with its root microbiota by releasing distinct coumarin chemotypes in response to environmental pH. These root-exuded specialized metabolites interact with root-associated bacteria to mobilize Fe either through bacterial siderophore-dependent chelation at circumneutral pH or through bacterial redox-sensing-controlled reduction at acidic pH.
n6ee197d04b69: We use PEtracer to reconstruct high-resolution lineage histories for >1.4 million cells from E7.5 to E10.0 during mouse development, providing a quantitative view of fate bias, restriction timing, and clonal output. Across diverse tissues, these data reveal highly reproducible lineage architectures and define general and tissue-specific strategies of cell fate specification.
n0d1670e68318: By destabilizing the endothelium and promoting macrophage lipid loading and inflammation, GIMAP6 deficiency drives atherosclerosis and ischemic heart disease through a mechanism that operates without hyperlipidemia, yet hyperlipidemia significantly exacerbates disease progression.
n84855d3dac90: Autophagy is impaired in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Zhang et al. identify a BRD4-BD1-selective inhibitor that disrupts BRD4-BD1–p62 engagement, restores protective autophagy, and attenuates pulmonary fibrosis, revealing a druggable mechanism linking epigenetic regulation to autophagy.
n1ae4ba90fdd9: Wang et al. map >1,000 interactions between Salmonella isolates and bacteriophages to measure the relative contributions of surface features and intracellular defense to phage resistance across a major human pathogen. They further identify AppA, which blocks DNA packaging by targeting the large terminase and restricts phage replication within mammalian hosts.
n3770519e460d: Whole-genome sequencing has revealed hundreds of cancer driver mutations in protein-coding genes, while our knowledge of how non-coding mutations contribute to tumorigenesis remains limited. Here, we develop and perform large-scale functional screens to identify non-coding regulatory elements whose mutations drive cancer development in non-transformed human breast epithelial cells and mouse models of breast and skin cancer. We identify 12 frequently mutated regulatory elements associated with 16 genes as candidate cancer drivers. Mechanistically, we characterize two elements associated with the microRNA MIR21 and the tumor suppressor gene, ZFP36L2. Mutating these regulatory elements dysregulates the expression of MIR21 and ZFP36L2, thereby leading to oncogenic transformation. We identify ZFP36L2 as a p53 target gene and find that mutating the p53-binding motif in the ZFP36L2 promoter is sufficient to drive tumorigenesis. Conceptually, our data indicate that cancer driver mutations in non-coding regulatory elements are much more prevalent and potent than initially assumed.
n188bc89ec706: Hybridization and introgression can promote speciation and phenotypic diversity. We investigated genomic divergence between two closely related Asian songbirds, Naumann's Thrush (Turdus naumanni, Nau) and Dusky Thrush (T. eunomus, Eun), and their evolutionary relationship with the geographically adjacent Red-throated Thrush (T. ruficollis, Ruf). Utilizing a de novo chromosome-level genome and whole-genome resequencing data from 66 individuals, we characterized differentiation and introgression among the three species. Genomic divergence between Nau and Eun was restricted to a few genomic islands that overlap with regions introgressed into Nau from Ruf. Notably, these regions harbor three melanin-related genes under strong selection in Nau (ASIP, OCA2, and HERC2), which may account for the plumage similarity between Nau and Ruf. These findings suggest that the morphological and genetic divergence between Nau and Eun may have been driven by adaptive introgression of melanin-related genes from Ruf into Nau. This study reveals how introgression can generate rapid genomic and phenotypic divergence, indicating a potentially ubiquitous yet overlooked speciation mechanism.
n6bc7a33732fc: Quan et al. construct a spatiotemporal transcriptomic atlas of radiation-induced brain injury and show that loss of radiosensitive Tmsb4x+ choroid plexus epithelial cells triggers blood-CSF barrier dysfunction and macrophage infiltration that sustains interferon-responsive microglial activation. These findings position the blood-CSF barrier as a potential target for mitigating post-irradiation neuroinflammation.
n251339339d19: Delplanque et al. combine large-scale human genetics with functional analyses to reassess the role of NCOA1 in obesity. Despite its biological plausibility within the melanocortin pathway, pathogenic NCOA1 variants were not associated with adiposity, questioning their relevance for precision obesity therapies targeting this pathway.
n7320728e92b5: Zhao et al. attach multiple lipid motifs to antibody-based biologic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (bDMARDs), enabling them to engage multiple albumin molecules in vivo and enhancing their accumulation in inflamed joints and lymph nodes. This generalizable strategy can target therapeutics larger than albumin to inflammatory sites for improved rheumatoid arthritis treatment.
n828e34d4d769: Deng et al. show that reduced preoperative fecal naringenin and β-glucuronidase activity associate with postoperative acute gastrointestinal injury after cardiopulmonary bypass. Mechanistically, microbial β-glucuronidase promotes naringenin release and limits epithelial ferroptosis, highlighting candidate noninvasive biomarkers and a potential microbiota-based intervention axis.
n401b49bfa630: Chen et al. track cfDNA methylation during neoadjuvant immunochemoradiotherapy for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Methylation signals decline with treatment and are associated with pathological response and disease-free survival. The decline is reproduced in a separate 30-patient cohort, supporting further evaluation of cfDNA methylation for noninvasive monitoring.
naabe3db7abde: Forcados et al. develop and test a combinatorial CAR strategy against B cell lymphoma, in which they combine CD75s and CD19 targeting. This combinatorial approach overcomes the limited efficiency of CD75s mono-targeting and lowers the risk of CAR-related toxicity seen with CD19 single targeting.
n52209105b49d: Alcohol’s brain effects are attributed to neurons, leaving microglial functional involvement untested. Paouri, Stanko, et al. show that microglia drive alcohol-induced sedation, motor impairment, and synaptic and neuronal loss through MyD88-dependent perisynaptic extracellular matrix (ECM) disruption. Equivalent neuron-targeted sedation bypassing microglia spares the ECM. Brain ECM loss also marks human alcohol use disorder, identifying a therapeutic target distinct from neuronal interventions.
n72ded1edb14f: Duan et al. solved the structure of ATRX ATPase-nucleosome complex, uncovering three distinctive features that enable ATRX to remodel nucleosomes. These newly identified features are indispensable for protecting cells from G4 stress. The work provides a framework for interpreting both known and future mutations linked to ATRX-related disorders.
n4cfe54d95549: Roots navigate soils where abiotic cues intersect with microbial activity. How they extract directional information from microbial processes remains unclear. Bao et al. identify saprotropism, whereby decay-generated pH gradients steer roots via the root meristem growth factor (RGF)–RGF receptor–abscisic acid signaling, revealing how ecological complexity shapes developmental decisions.
n091c1a5c9ab4: Enhancer of zeste homolog 2 (EZH2) is the catalytic subunit of Polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2), which mediates transcriptional repression. Kim and colleagues uncover a PRC2-independent EZH2-sterol regulatory element-binding protein 2 (SREBP2) axis that drives cholesterol biosynthesis, revealing an epigenetic-metabolic vulnerability exploitable through targeted protein degradation.
n7945c9e6b5a0: Peripheral neuropathy is a poorly understood yet extraordinarily relevant obstacle to the effective implementation of cytotoxic chemotherapy in patients with cancer. Recent findings from Heles et al. demonstrate that safe neuroactive molecules that promote mitochondrial fitness in axons effectively prevent peripheral neuropathy in preclinical tumor models, thereby supporting clinical translation.
n20e85efa077a: Reversible protein S-acylation regulates immune checkpoint function. Zhang et al. demonstrate that ZDHHC15-mediated S-acylation stabilizes CD155, whereas genetic or pharmacological disruption promotes CD155 degradation, enhances anti-tumor immunity, and suppresses tumor growth.
n87a4d92b6ce7: Wang et al. develop a standardized reaggregated glioblastoma organoid (rGBO) platform that enables scalable evaluation of patient-specific treatment responses. The platform links organoid radiosensitivity with patient survival, identifies response-related transcriptomic signatures, and reveals BET inhibition as a strategy to enhance radiotherapy efficacy in organoid and xenograft models.
n3a5c8238e83c: Chen et al. establish a translational functional pipeline to reclassify OTOF variants of uncertain significance. This pipeline enables definitive molecular diagnosis and eligibility for gene therapy trials; it further reveals that K1992R drives pathogenicity in the E1700Q haplotype via disrupting otoferlin localization.
nabb83bed762d: Yang et al. demonstrate, in primates, that a fusion-loop-engineered Zika mRNA vaccine confers full protection with negligible dengue ADE. The response is dominated by convergent B cells orthologous to human IGHV5-10-1 whose antibodies target a distinct viral hotspot, with DENV envelope N67-linked glycan preventing cross-reactivity for safer flavivirus vaccines.
n206f73fb3eb1: Zhao et al. investigate the role of the tongue microbiome in prediabetes and glycemic dysregulation. Rothia mucilaginosa and microbial nitrate metabolism are associated with lower prediabetes prevalence and improve the prediction of prediabetes progression, highlighting oral nitrate metabolism as a potential modifiable link between the oral microbiome and metabolic health.
n180405b67c3b: Lee et al. integrate structural brain MRI with plasma proteomics to identify a three-region brain age model that predicts mortality more accurately than global measures and reveals shared immune and vascular mechanisms. These findings support regional brain aging as a scalable biomarker for precision geromedicine.
n2b92f8f7be3e: Tsai et al. discover that ribosome composition is reprogrammed in response to intrinsic and external cellular perturbations, which supports ribosome remodeling as a conserved mechanism that enables adaptive protein synthesis during pathogen infection and cellular adaptation.
n41909eaeb9fe: Interpretability must be a first-class design objective for the next generation of foundation models in molecular biology. In this perspective, Varma and Ideker examine the ways in which it can be built into a model, from biological priors to architecture, and provide a checklist for authors and reviewers.
n00285d811641: The emergence of tumor-agnostic therapies has fundamentally transformed precision oncology. Traditionally developed and approved for metastatic disease, nine therapies spanning immunotherapy, targeted agents, and antibody–drug conjugates now demonstrate a compelling rationale for earlier deployment in the neoadjuvant setting. This review examines the paradigm shift from last-resort to first-consideration approaches. Key advantages of neoadjuvant, biomarker-guided therapy include intervention prior to the development of therapeutic resistance, optimal immune system engagement, and opportunities for organ preservation. Single-agent programmed cell death protein-1 blockade has achieved a 100% complete response rate in mismatch repair-deficient rectal cancer with preserved organ function. Neurotrophic tyrosine receptor kinase (NTRK), rearranged during transfection (RET), and B-Raf proto-oncogene serine/threonine kinase (BRAF) inhibitors have demonstrated substantial responses that enable curative-intent surgery across malignancies. As precision oncology matures, the neoadjuvant tumor-agnostic approach exemplifies optimized therapeutic sequencing, potentially improving patient outcomes and quality of life.
na2d881469118: Huang and colleagues investigated how slow-paced breathing shapes physiological and brain-related signals during financial decisions under risk. Their findings elucidate neurovisceral pathways linking prolonged exhalation to increased risk-taking, whereby heightened cardiac parasympathetic modulation increases reward sensitivity and neural activity in brain regions involved in valuation and interoception.
ne2a2d1e28654: Glutathione (GSH) robustly defends against ferroptosis independently of GPX4. FSP1 utilizes GSH to reduce ubiquinone and subsequently inhibits ferroptosis, which is distinct from the NAD(P)H-FAD axis. Targeting the FSP1-GSH axis efficiently alleviated ferroptosis-induced tissue injury.
nbca19882c1bf: A 3D spatiotemporal cell atlas of rice spanning the entire seed-to-seed lifecycle. Developmental trajectories are captured, and the spatially distinct roles of OsARF1 in rice development and dorsoventral endosperm asymmetry related to starch and protein accumulation are revealed.
n406ba3350fa9: A CRISPR screen of solute carriers reveals that T cells depend on SLC52A3 for VB2 uptake, whereas tumors preferentially exploit SLC52A2 to outcompete them, thereby driving T cell ferroptosis. Enforced SLC52A3 overexpression in T cells reverses this metabolic competition and enhances their antitumor activity.
nb20d96d4db34: Current genetic screens face a trade-off between scaling to large mutant libraries and measuring information-rich phenotypes. SPARCS automates laser microdissection to enable pooled forward genetic screens for complex image-based phenotypes at scale. By physically recovering individual mutants, SPARCS supports multimodal profiling of hits beyond genotyping, including via mass spectrometry-based proteomics.
nd54c53353a98: Sex differences in antibody-based cancer therapy remain poorly understood. This study identifies estrogen-driven STING reprogramming and neutrophil extracellular trap formation as a mechanism of functional antigen shielding that limits ADC efficacy.
n1ba64eac5687: In this review, Walker et al. discuss how reactive metabolites can non-enzymatically modify proteins to shape immune cell function. They discuss mechanisms governing modification selectivity and regulation, emerging chemical biology tools to study these modifications, and how these modifications connect immunometabolism with inflammation, disease, and therapeutic opportunities.
n9a1afb308222: Chronic pain is a complex neurobiological problem whose solution is elusive. Powell et al. describe an approach to reduce chronic neuropathic pain in rodent models using a short lipidated peptide designed to inhibit the interaction between Nav1.8 and Ankyrin-3.
nba482f07c65e: Interleukin (IL)-10 produced by B cells has regulatory functions in disease contexts. Manfroi et al. report a strategy for the efficient generation of IL-10-producing B cells using a chemical compound identified through a high-throughput screen. Upon transfer, these IL-10+ B cells reverse ongoing CNS autoimmunity at disease peak in a manner dependent on IL-10 receptor expression in myeloid cells.
n3036f3850b62: Dossin et al. report that BRCA1 and BRCA2 deficiencies create distinct adaptive states. They identify FANCM-RMI1/2 as an opposing determinant of cell fitness: essential in BRCA1-deficient cells but toxic in BRCA2-deficient cells, where it drives replication fork degradation. Disrupting FANCM-RMI1/2 restores genome stability and promotes PARPi resistance in BRCA2-deficient cells.
na5e82be6fd33: Porat et al. develop cell surface ATAC-See, discovering that mitochondrial DNA is a component of the mammalian cell surface. Cell surface DNA (csDNA) on primary human and murine B cells and monocytes is removed by the secreted nuclease DNASE1L3, and dysregulation of csDNA levels is associated with autoimmunity.
nd91313ac5e95: Han et al. review how protein arginine methyltransferases (PRMTs) coordinate chromatin regulation, RNA metabolism, and immune signaling. They discuss emerging roles of PRMTs in tumor immunity and inflammaging and discuss catalytic and non-catalytic strategies for therapeutically targeting PRMT-dependent immune regulation.
n2f5ab4e06584: Bushnell, Schulz, and Villada introduce RandomReadsMG, a fast simulator that generates metagenomic sequencing datasets with controlled community abundance, uneven genome coverage, and platform-specific read properties. The software scales to communities of 50,000 genomes and supports reproducible benchmarking and pathogen-detection study design.
nf5f277fbc000: Vasquez et al. use high-resolution lineage tracking to follow tens of thousands of Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron lineages in the mouse gut. They show that rapid evolution can overcome colonization resistance, enabling adaptive strains to spread between hosts, while community diversity reshapes the evolutionary landscape without preventing adaptation and transmission.
n0859296f5f68: Xu et al. show that blocking the CD47-SIRPα phagocytic checkpoint paradoxically elevates tumor-derived PCSK9, which degrades MHC-I on macrophages and impairs antigen cross-presentation to CD8+ T cells. A bispecific fusion protein co-targeting CD47 and PCSK9 overcomes this resistance, restoring T cell priming and achieving tumor control with improved safety.
nbbc575b8a250: Suzawa and Qiu et al. identify “two-factor authorization” of post-transcriptional gene regulation by germline-specific RNA-binding proteins DND1 and NANOS3. As a complex, the two proteins with low (DND1) and no (NANOS3) sequence specificity select targets with a unique 3′ UTR to collaboratively repress expression of cell cycle and epigenetic regulators.
nbaa869f17b16: Intramembrane proteases catalyze peptide bond hydrolysis within cellular membranes, regulating processes including signaling, protein quality control, and membrane protein turnover. Recent advances in cryo-electron microscopy, biochemistry, and molecular dynamics simulations have transformed our understanding of how these enzymes recognize and process substrates within the lipid bilayer. Here, we discuss how dynamic interactions among proteases, substrates, and membranes govern substrate recognition. Structural and biophysical studies reveal how conformational dynamics, membrane remodeling, and specific protease–substrate interactions enable processing of membrane-embedded substrates. Studies of rhomboid pseudoproteases further suggest that transmembrane-domain recognition represents a conserved principle of membrane protein processing that extends beyond proteolysis itself. Finally, we consider how recognition determines membrane protein fate, linking protease activity to signaling, proteostasis, and nonproteolytic scaffolding functions.
nef40f51d57ea: The acoustic signal of speech is fleeting and unfolds linearly; yet listeners must derive temporally extended and hierarchically organized linguistic structures to comprehend it. This article reviews evidence that the human brain transforms the transient auditory signal into neural representations that are persistent, parallel, and time-stamped. First, neural persistence allows information to remain available after it has disappeared from the acoustic input. Second, parallel encoding of recent inputs across multiple levels of language structure enables composition and interactions across the speech hierarchy. Third, dynamic neural representations encode both content and elapsed time, providing a flexible mechanism for preserving sequence order. Together, these representational properties reveal how the human brain transforms a continuously disappearing signal into temporally extended linguistic structures.
n4e0e2a4ccafa: Pharmacological studies of GPCRs are often complicated by off-target effects. Matsuoka et al. develop ESCAPE, a chemogenetic platform that preserves endogenous ligand responsiveness while eliminating antagonist sensitivity, enabling receptor-specific interrogation of GPCR signaling in cells and physiological models.
n6a4274a2734e: Cha and Kim review two decades of iPSC-based translation in neurodegenerative disease, highlighting disease-specific therapeutic logic and the emerging importance of transplantation biology. They propose a phase-resolved framework for the post-transplant “biological black box” linking graft survival, maturation, host interactions, and long-term therapeutic outcome.
nb9d416db80bc: Sheng et al. integrate spatial multi-omics, functional models, and clinical validation to show that fibrotic stroma suppresses epithelial cGAS-STING signaling and T cell recruitment in HCC. Their GCSS model links tumor architecture to response prediction for TACE plus immune checkpoint blockade.
n1b770c6d3bbb: Ferman et al. demonstrate that epigenetic imbalance directly controls MYC oncogene amplification dynamics, which identifies possible biomarkers and therapeutic targets for aggressive tumors. When a cell-death checkpoint fails, the low MYC copy gains expand to high levels, which include circular and integrated events and associate with tumorigenesis.
n483073cdd5ad: Hepatic FoxO1 is a promising therapeutic target for hyperglycemia. Gong et al. show that hepatic FoxO1 loss derepresses Cers2/4 transcription, increasing liver-derived C18/22/24 ceramides that promote pancreatic β cell apoptosis. These findings reveal an inter-organ signaling pathway with implications for FoxO1-targeting antihyperglycemic therapies.
n30eaade0b004: Jo et al. show that transient OSKM induction generates two distinct liver progenitor-like cell populations with limited immune activation. Liver-targeted OSKM mRNA-LNPs induce hepatocyte dedifferentiation and enhance regeneration after acetaminophen-induced liver injury, supporting transient hepatic reprogramming as a strategy for inducing regenerative plasticity with therapeutic potential for acute injury.
n2e63b71a0f3e: Menzel, Zhou, et al. examine the impact of surgical removal of tumor-draining lymph node (tdLN) resection on anti-tumor immunity. They find that after tdLN resection, tumor antigen is rerouted to distant LNs, where it supports tumor-specific T cell responses and immune checkpoint blockade efficacy. Targeting these compensatory LNs enhances anti-cancer immunity after lymph node surgery.
ne88a1c245e40: Messemaker et al. develop a TCR rapid assembly platform (T-RAP) and use it to generate a large high-quality dataset of functionally validated TCR-pMHC pairs. With the resulting validated TCR-pMHC dataset (TCRvdb), structure-based prediction of TCR-pMHC reactivity is more feasible than previously assumed.
na6a01e231d86: Glucose deprivation in the solid tumor microenvironment impairs T cell persistence, but the mechanisms remain unclear. Fu et al. identified an AMPK-ZAK-NIK axis activated by glucose deprivation in Th9 cells that inhibits IL-9 secretion, triggering cell senescence and impaired persistence. ZAK targeting rejuvenates Th9 cells, consequently boosting the anti-tumor potency of CAR-Th9-based therapies for solid tumors.
ne8283817eb4b: Cell-free RNA (cfRNA) is emerging as a promising analyte for liquid biopsy because it captures dynamic changes in gene expression across tissues and disease states. However, interpretation of cfRNA profiles remains limited by the lack of a unifying framework describing how extracellular RNAs are released, processed, and stabilized. Here, we propose that concepts from cell-free DNA fragmentomics provide a useful lens to interpret cfRNA biology and introduce the concept of cfRNA fragmentomics. We argue that many cfRNAs originate as intracellular ribonucleoprotein complexes that undergo extracellular ribonuclease processing, generating stable fragmented RNAs associated with proteins and other carriers. Under this framework, informative cfRNA signatures may arise not only from diseased tissues but also from indirect systemic responses to disease.
na22fd6053780: Protein tyrosine phosphatases (PTPs) are increasingly recognized as regulators of signaling networks rather than mere antagonists of kinases. Interactome-level analyses reveal that many PTPs function as scaffolds that organize spatially constrained signaling complexes, thereby influencing context-dependent signaling outputs. Focusing on representative nonreceptor PTPs (SHP-2, PTPN23, and PTPN13) and receptor PTPs (PTPRM and PTPRK), this review integrates methodological advances that enable increasingly detailed mapping of PTP-centered interactomes. Across cancer, neurobiology, and immune signaling, changes in these assemblies link scaffold function to disease phenotypes. This framework highlights PTP scaffold functions beyond catalysis and emerging therapeutic strategies targeting protein–protein interactions and scaffold-dependent mechanisms.
nfb2b179ad109: Cohesin organizes genome folding through loop extrusion, a process regulated by cofactors including NIPBL and PDS5. Recent studies by Wutz et al. and Shah et al. demonstrate that NIPBL promotes loop expansion in mammalian cells, whereas PDS5 restricts loop growth by facilitating NIPBL dissociation from cohesin. Together, these findings reveal a finely tuned mechanism governing genome folding.
n286715392117: The immune signal SA triggers metabolic changes to activate SnRK1 while inhibiting TOR. These central metabolic kinases antagonistically phosphorylate the key immune regulator NPR1, thereby coupling cellular metabolic state to systemic acquired resistance.
n0a858991fff7: Proteolysis limits the therapeutic use of peptide antibiotics. Wang et al. develop C12RP7, a fatty-acid-modified Arg-Pro lipopeptide that resists proteases, kills antibiotic-resistant bacteria, shows low toxicity and resistance propensity, and provides oral efficacy through bacterial membrane disruption and host metabolic modulation.
n92dbceef93a1: An oral enzyme-responsive co-delivery nanoplatform is designed to achieve controlled release of tryptophan and the metabolism inhibitor NLG919, specifically in the large intestine. This design redirects tryptophan metabolism toward immunostimulatory microbial indole derivative production, while blocking the immunosuppressive kynurenine pathway, thereby synergistically eliciting robust antitumor immunity in colorectal cancer.
n82e3b485dd84: German et al. use integrated multi-omics analysis to identify EZH2 as a central regulator of prostate cancer phenotypic plasticity. The study reveals TTP-associated pathways and adaptive PI3K/mTORC1 as mediators of response to EZH2 inhibition and demonstrates that co-targeting EZH2 and PI3K/mTORC1 is an effective strategy in aggressive prostate cancer models.
n10275fd2c4f5: Fu and Ma et al. develop DVH to edit DCs into CCR7+IL-7+ DCs, which target the T-zone within TDLNs and secrete IL-7 to promote Tscm differentiation. The Tscms can self-renew and generate effector T cells under antigen stimulation continuously, thereby killing tumor cells and reducing T cell exhaustion at the source.
n51a4323d2eb1: The autoimmune regulator (Aire) promotes T cell tolerance through promiscuous gene expression in medullary thymic epithelial cells, but growing evidence suggests that it has functions beyond its canonical role in thymic tolerance. Sayed et al. demonstrate that Aire acts as a cell-intrinsic regulator of T-independent natural IgM-secreting cells, homeostatically restraining their number and natural IgM abundance.
n08670039e4d5: Childhood maltreatment shapes brain development in ways that vary by adversity type, developmental timing, and genetic vulnerability to psychiatric illness—a heterogeneity that conventional approaches capture poorly. We contend that normative modeling, multivariate methods, and polygenic risk scores offer complementary frameworks for parsing this variability and advancing mechanistic insights and clinical stratification.
n0a797f710b92: Indole-producing Escherichia coli worsens ischemic stroke through the activation of aryl hydrocarbon receptor signaling in dendritic cells. Limiting AHR signaling in DCs promotes gut-derived DC migration to the meninges, expands meningeal regulatory T cells, and reduces neuroinflammation. This microbiota-AHR axis offers a promising therapeutic target.
ne815a7b70b0b: In a large, real-world mixed-cancer cohort, analyses accounting for comorbidities and additional confounders indicate that most microbiome alterations are shared across cancers rather than specific to individual cancers. Distinct associations are limited to a subset of cancers and, in separate analyses, to age of onset and specific treatment-related adverse events.
nf3f26930f0c8: Pancreatic cancer cachexia is accompanied by progressive assembly of a spatially organized tumor-macrophage-fibroblast niche. Reciprocal signaling among the cellular populations in the niche is associated with muscle wasting and cachexia progression.
ndda6eae69ffe: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) generate protein structure and function diversity. Advances in mass spectrometry have revealed numerous bacterial PTMs, increasing the need to understand their functional purpose. Dale et al. review these modifications and examine their evolving roles in bacterial physiology and pathogenesis.
n83afb2dc30cd: Lin and Li et al. expose differentiating human stem cell cultures to nicotine, caffeine, or ethanol and identify genetic variants whose effects on gene expression emerge only after exposure. These context-specific regulatory variants resemble disease-associated loci, illustrating how environment-sensitive gene regulation can help explain signals from human genetic studies.
nf8a76d33e458: Van Renne, Agostinetto, et al. perform a multi-omics characterization of advanced TNBC to identify response predictors and treatment-induced dynamics during chemo-ICI. Poor outcomes are associated with fibrovascular and myeloid remodeling, highlighting coordinated resistance mechanisms, actionable therapeutic targets, and the value of microenvironment-based stratification for future ICI-based trials.
nf9887fc520a1: Guan et al. develop an IAA-assisted engineered bacterial therapy for pancreatic cancer. IAA suppresses neutrophil recruitment and synergizes with gemcitabine to eliminate neutrophils, boosting bacterial colonization and antitumor immune efficacy.
n713c0e3faf7a: Circumventricular organs are specialized brain regions lacking a blood-brain barrier. Van Hove et al. reveal that these regions harbor unique microglia and border-associated macrophage populations that respond to ageing and metabolism and are partly derived from fetal monocytes entering during a perinatal window, which can fully adopt the microglia identity.
n8dc7f4be2b82: Le Rest et al. identify ZC3H18 as the long-sought molecular link between the cap-binding complex (CBC) and first intron splicing. ZC3H18 recruits early splicing factors through interactions that are mutually exclusive with RNA decay factor binding, implying how cap-bound nascent transcripts are directed toward productive splicing rather than degradation.
n1b30a9103c30: Cadar et al. show that the transcription factor Dorsal forms clusters at genes carrying many binding sites in living fly embryos. Losing these clusters is lethal, yet they do not switch genes on; they merely boost output from already-active genes, challenging prevailing views of how condensates control transcription.
n254104965196: Belyaeva and Elgeti present an integrative modeling pipeline for proteins that combines experimental DEER data with deep-learning techniques and short molecular dynamics simulations. Application to the important drug target AT1R yields all-atom models of previously unknown conformations, which can be used to develop safer therapeutics.
ne07f80f30182: Salar et al. use molecular dynamics simulations and biochemical analyses to show how dynamics within the GacS S-helix facilitates interactions with RetS and regulate signal transmission to the kinase domain. These findings establish a novel model for the regulation of GacS and thus of virulence gene expression in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
n550ddea24380: Cargo has traditionally been viewed as a passive substrate of coat-mediated transport. Cryo-EM reveals that cargo containing tandem sorting motifs directly promotes higher-order adaptor assembly by bridging AP-1 complexes, enabling efficient trafficking and neuronal development in zebrafish.
nc0122016561b: Remote activation of a single-AAV-deliverable photoswitchable Cas12f system enables precise spatial and temporal control of genome editing in deep tissues without surgery or implanted devices.
n1252fce75a0f: Gut microbial taxonomy alone is a poor predictor of CAR-T cell therapy outcome. Instead, specific gut immunomodulatory metabolites exert opposing effects on CAR-T cell function and tumor control, identifying microbial metabolism as a potential target to predict and improve CAR-T cell outcomes.
nfb8d98b70524: Integrin inhibitors are drugs designed to block cell adhesion, but they have repeatedly failed in clinical trials. Lee et al. show that these drugs cannot inhibit a newly discovered adhesion structure, curved adhesions, and therefore fail to block cancer cell invasion in 3D, potentially explaining some previous clinical failures.
n5583da884b78: Anderson et al. compare brain gene regulation across nine mammals, revealing that enhancer conservation extends beyond DNA sequence to include cell-type specificity and gene targets. Functional assays show how both ancient and human-specific regulatory elements shape brain biology and susceptibility to neurologic disease.
n4b834c2aa6a7: Handal et al. isolate a panel of naturally occurring human monoclonal antibodies against the measles fusion protein that potently neutralize in vitro and inhibit viral replication in vivo, demonstrating strong clinical potential. Two antibodies bind distinct portions of the F protein simultaneously with epitopes spanning across multiple F protomers.
n81a7556d1d3f: Chen et al. identify two neutralizing antibodies, G4 and B9, targeting distinct epitopes on the mpox virus M1R protein (an L1R homolog). Despite targeting a conventional epitope, G4 overcomes Asp35-associated neutralization escape. Both antibodies protect against multiple orthopoxviruses in vitro and in vivo, supporting their potential as broad-spectrum antiviral candidates.
n083c5b866830: Sommerova et al. show that ataxia telangiectasia-mutated (ATM) protects replicating cells by restraining pathological bypass of endogenous oxidative base lesions through PRIMPOL-mediated repriming. When ATM is lost, post-replicative adducted ssDNA gaps accumulate, creating dependence on homologous recombination for repair and driving PARP hyperactivation and PARP inhibitor sensitivity.
nb2b925bcc4c8: Cryo-electron tomography has emerged as a powerful technology for in-cell structural biology and, in combination with breakthroughs in protein structure prediction, offers a unique opportunity for illuminating functions of previously uncharacterized macromolecular complexes. Here, we used the genome-reduced bacterium Mycoplasma pneumoniae as a minimal cell model and determined in-cell maps of an unknown complex located at the cell surface. By combining proteomics, structure prediction, integrative modeling, and bioinformatics, we identified the complex to include the conserved Sec-translocon and an extracellular dome-like structure largely formed by three uncharacterized proteins (Mdps). The Mdps show structural homology to the periplasmic ATP-independent foldase PrsA, with Mdp444 retaining key catalytic residues and activity. Our study provides the first sub-nanometer-resolution maps of the complete bacterial Sec-translocation machinery, depicting its association in SecA-mediated co-translational translocation and its coordination with an extracellular protein-folding system.
nb789e849a8e0: Translation is a central process in gene expression. Its regulation is complex, depends on factors that include cell state and the subcellular environment, and is subject to modulation via crosstalk to processes such as transcription or translocation. Here, we used cryo-electron tomography of native and antibiotic-perturbed Mycoplasma pneumoniae cells to resolve 140 maps that recapitulate bacterial translation during the initiation, elongation, and recycling phases. We visualized multiple transcription-translation complexes, allowing us to propose a threading-based translation reinitiation mechanism and to provide structural evidence for a long-hypothesized supercomplex that coordinates transcription, translation, and membrane attachment. We resolved abundant membrane-associated large ribosomal subunits and suggest that dissociation from membranes depends on the conditional initiation of new translation, consistent with a potentially conserved mechanism in mammalian cells. This work visualizes the multilayered control of bacterial translation and demonstrates the power of in-cell structural biology to investigate regulatory circuits in gene expression.
nb3a1fa840c6a: Fusarium pathogens deploy mycotoxins as virulence factors to promote disease progression in cereal crops, leading to yield loss and food contamination. However, how mycotoxins interact with crops remains unknown. Here, we discover that mycotoxin deoxynivalenol (DON) hijacks multiple wheat nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD)+-dependent metabolic enzymes, disrupting glycolytic and TCA-cycle homeostasis, thereby contributing to Fusarium head blight (FHB) susceptibility. In this context, we identify that myo-inositol-1-phosphate synthase (MIPS), one DON interactor, redirects myo-inositol-phosphoinositide metabolism, promoting DON transport into vacuoles in a phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PI(4,5)P2)-dependent manner. This sequestration counteracts DON's cytoplasmic hijacking, preventing host central metabolic disruption and FHB development. Increasing MIPS expression in wheat and maize confers broad resistance to Fusarium diseases without agronomic penalty in field trials, rescuing up to 43% yield loss and reducing up to 88% DON accumulation in grain. Our findings reveal a metabolic "hijacking-counteracting" framework in plant-mycotoxin interactions, providing a robust strategy for improving crop disease resistance and mycotoxin management.
n401812dfeb1d: Myocardial infarction (MI) remains a leading cause of death worldwide, and therapies that limit injury, promote repair, and restore cardiac function remain limited. Human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) provide a renewable source of patient-specific cardiac cells and have enabled the development of increasingly complex in vitro models that incorporate cardiomyocytes together with supporting stromal and vascular cell types. These models are now being used to study multiple stages of MI pathophysiology and are increasingly being applied in therapeutic discovery and regenerative strategies. In this review, we summarize hiPSC-based cardiac models spanning 2D cultures to advanced 3D tissues, organoids, and heart-on-chip systems, evaluating how well they capture key features of human MI. We further discuss hiPSC applications in therapeutic discovery, drug screening, precision medicine, and regenerative repair. Finally, we highlight priorities for the field, including improved physiological complexity, stronger translational robustness, bioengineering strategies, and integration with multi-omics.
n25ec6cc6a76c: ROR1 is expressed across a broad spectrum of malignancies. While T lymphocytes armed with chimeric antigen receptor targeting ROR1 (CART-ROR1 cells) have reached clinical stage, the efficacy of this therapy has been limited. We report that inhibition of H3K27 methyltransferase EZH2 and, to a much lesser degree, the DNA methyltransferase DNMT1 and the H3K9 methyltransferase G9A promotes ROR1 expression by malignant cells. EZH2 inhibition also directly impairs the growth of some malignant cell populations. The combination of EZH2 inhibition and CART-ROR1 cells is much more effective than CART-ROR1 cells alone in eliminating malignant cells. While EZH2 inhibition variably enhances the expression of immune checkpoint receptors, it markedly increases the synthesis of T cell-activating soluble factors and promotes the cytotoxic phenotype of CART-ROR1 cells. These results indicate that EZH2 inhibition enhances the CART-ROR1 cell effectiveness by diverse mechanisms, including promotion of ROR1 expression by malignant cells, suggesting that the combination may prove clinically more effective than CART-ROR1 cell monotherapy.
n467c56543774: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes substantial respiratory disease, while treatment is limited by drug resistance. Molecular docking of a 3,880-compound natural-product library identifies punicalin (PUN) as a dual-target RSV entry inhibitor. PUN inhibits the evaluated RSV-A and RSV-B strains, including a clinical isolate, and retains activity against strains resistant to ziresovir, ribavirin, nirsevimab, and palivizumab. After 20 passages under PUN selection, the half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) increases 3.88-fold, remaining below the predefined >10-fold resistance threshold. Mechanistic analyses suggest that PUN interacts with the G protein cystine-noose region involving N178, N179, and W183 to inhibit attachment and with an F protein region involving V243, T245, and P246 to stabilize prefusion F and inhibit membrane fusion. These regions do not overlap known resistance hotspots. In RSV-infected mice, nebulized PUN provides sustained respiratory exposure, reduces lung viral loads and pathology, and attenuates inflammatory responses.
nbc72c34356e1: Induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived retinal organoids (ROs) have emerged as a platform for photoreceptor replacement therapy, supported by two complementary approaches: cone precursor cell transplantation and RO transplantation. Both have demonstrated proof of concept for functional synaptic integration with the host retinal network, with the first clinical application of iPSC-derived RO transplantation conducted in 2020. Key mechanistic insights include the role of the host environment in cone integration, genome editing-based enhancement of host-graft synaptogenesis recapitulating developmental synaptic assembly, and synaptic rewiring capacity in the adult primate retina. Beyond biology, successful clinical translation requires establishing meaningful endpoints that reflect stepwise therapeutic improvement, scalable good manufacturing practice (GMP)-compliant manufacturing including validated preservation protocols, and regulatory frameworks accommodating progenitor-stage cell therapies. Together, these advances offer a realistic path toward vision restoration in patients with currently untreatable retinal degenerative diseases.
ne09914b78c4f: Importins transport numerous proteins into cell nuclei. They also chaperone highly positively charged cargoes against ionic aggregation during transit. An extreme example is histone H1, which requires two importins, Importin 7 (Imp7) and Importin β (Impβ), for safe import. Here, we present a combined cryoelectron microscopy (cryo-EM)/molecular dynamics (MD) structure of the Imp7·Impβ·H1 complex, correcting a previous model (PDB 6N88) with misassigned importin chains. Our structure reveals that Imp7 contacts Impβ via three interfaces and that this heterodimerization creates a large negatively charged cavity. The globular H1-domain is recognized by Imp7 alone. The highly cationic C-terminal H1-tail participates in fluid-like transient interactions, contacting the inner surface of Impβ before returning to the α-solenoid and long acidic loop of Imp7. This architecture and dynamics explain how the importins shield the histone's enormous positive charge while avoiding interactions too strong for efficient intranuclear cargo release. Finally, we report a RanGTP·Imp7 structure, illustrating how RanGTP dissociates the import complex inside nuclei.
n8b852db59de3: Cerebrovascular disease is a major but poorly understood feature of Alzheimer's disease (AD). The strongest genetic AD risk factor, apolipoprotein E4 (APOE4), is associated with cerebrovascular degeneration, including vascular amyloid deposition and fibrosis. To uncover how APOE4 promotes cerebrovascular pathology, we assembled a single-cell transcriptomic atlas of human brain vasculature. In APOE4 carriers, pericyte abundance was significantly reduced and accompanied by the emergence of a myofibroblast-like cell population co-expressing contraction and extracellular matrix genes. Immunostaining confirmed non-vascular myofibroblasts in APOE4 human and mouse brains. We show that APOE4 pericytes transition into myofibroblasts that secrete fibronectin, which promotes vascular amyloid accumulation. Computational and experimental analyses identified elevated transforming growth factor β (TGF-β) signaling as the driver of this pericyte-to-myofibroblast transition. Inhibition of TGF-β restored pericyte coverage and reduced vascular fibrosis and amyloid to APOE3 levels, revealing a targetable mechanism linking APOE4 to cerebrovascular pathology in AD.
n75ac17563a51: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), an aggressive cancer with a poor prognosis, contains resident tissue macrophages (RTMs) present before tumor onset and monocyte-derived macrophages recruited during tumor development, but their distinct roles in supporting tumor progression remain unclear. Combining single-cell profiling, spatial analysis, lineage tracing, RTM depletion, and selenium tracing, we found that RTMs preferentially localize at the tumor border, where they promote epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), tumor growth, and metastasis. Mechanistically, RTMs transfer the selenium transporter Selenop to EMThi tumor cells through LRP8-dependent uptake, increasing tumor-cell selenium availability, limiting lipid peroxidation, and shielding EMThi tumor cells from ferroptosis. RTM-specific Selenop deletion or tumor-cell Lrp8 disruption reduced EMT and tumor progression, whereas ferroptosis inhibition reversed the effect of RTM depletion. Human PDAC showed border-enriched SEPP1+ RTMs near EMThi tumor cells, suggesting a conserved macrophage-derived selenium niche that supports invasive tumor states and highlighting the potential for targeting RTMs or their secretory factors in PDAC.
nda92a5c2edc4: Heterochrony, or the alteration of developmental timing, is an important mechanism of evolutionary change. Avian species display synchronized growth of the forelimbs and hindlimbs, while mammalian species show delayed hindlimb development. We find that mammalian limb heterochrony is evident from the start of limb bud formation and is associated with heterochronic expression of T-box transcription factors. This heterochronic shift is not due to changes in cis-regulatory sequences controlling T-box gene expression but, unexpectedly, is dependent upon the differential oxygen levels to which avian and mammalian embryos are exposed prior to limb initiation. This is mediated, at least partially, by cRel, a transcription factor in the nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) family, and by the oxygen-sensing transcription factor hypoxia-inducible factor alpha (Hif1a). Together, these results provide a mechanistic understanding of an important example of developmental heterochrony and exemplify how the maternal environment can regulate timing during embryonic development.
nbc3cc1a41626: Metagenome sequencing has revolutionized functional microbiome analysis across diverse ecosystems but is fraught with technical hurdles. We introduce MOSHPIT (MOdular SHotgun metagenome Pipelines with Integrated provenance Tracking; https://moshpit.qiime2.org)-software built on the QIIME 2/rachis framework (Q2F) that integrates best-in-class CAMI II- and LEMMI-validated metagenome tools with robust provenance tracking and multiple user interfaces-enabling streamlined, reproducible metagenome analysis for all expertise levels. By building on Q2F, MOSHPIT enhances scalability, interoperability, and reproducibility in complex workflows, democratizing and accelerating discovery at the frontiers of metagenomics.
ne4beacee43f0: Immunosuppressive therapies (ISTs), including calcineurin inhibitors like cyclosporine A (CsA), are essential therapeutics for autoimmunity; however, they often fail and cause dose-limiting toxicity. Severe aplastic anemia (SAA) is a fatal autoimmune bone marrow (BM) failure disorder that is treated with ISTs. BM single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) from SAA patients reveals enhanced T cell effector programs, maladaptive myelopoiesis, and impaired inflammation resolution despite standard-of-care therapy, suggesting incomplete restoration of immune homeostasis with ISTs. In murine SAA, CsA improves survival but induces persistent inflammatory T cells, emergency myelopoiesis, and nephrotoxicity following withdrawal. The pro-resolving lipid mediator resolvin E1 (RvE1) similarly prevents SAA-induced mortality but without toxicity or persistent inflammation. Co-treatment with RvE1, concurrently or after CsA, achieves complete survival, restores immune and hematopoietic homeostasis, and reduces toxicity in a ChemR23-dependent manner. These findings support a paradigm shift toward curative therapies that simultaneously engage endogenous repair programs and suppress pathogenic responses to enhance treatment safety and durability.
nec006c8fe7a8: Shigellosis is the second leading cause of diarrheal death in children under 5 years globally, yet no licensed vaccine exists, partly due to poor understanding of protective immunity in young children, especially in endemic settings. Here, we applied a functional antibody-profiling approach to define Shigella-specific antibody responses in young children versus older individuals with culture-confirmed shigellosis in Bangladesh. We found that higher baseline O-specific polysaccharide (OSP)-specific and protein-specific IgG and FcγR binding levels correlated with less severe disease regardless of age. We also found that over time, individuals under 5 years of age developed a less functional and durable response against OSP than older individuals. We demonstrate that OSP-specific IgG increased uptake of live Shigella by monocytes and macrophages in an Fc-dependent mechanism. Our findings suggest that young children develop limited OSP-specific functional antibody responses that fail to maximally involve innate immune cells. Innate cell clearance may be important in protecting against Shigella.
nef1eaeb84f7e: Moyamoya disease (MMD) lacks reliable biomarkers for distinguishing it from atherosclerotic cerebrovascular disease (ACVD) and predicting postoperative collateral formation (PCF).
